title: Etale and Zariski cohomology of quasi-coherent modules agree, naturally in the module
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] let $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] be the associated etale sheaf $u\mapsto\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$ of [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], and for an $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\varphi_{\mathrm{et}}:\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal G_{\mathrm{et}}$ be given on an object $u:U\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ by $\Gamma(U,u^*\varphi):\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal G)$, where $u^*$ is the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $\varphi_{\mathrm{et}}$ is a morphism of $\Ab(X_{\Et})$, and there are isomorphisms of abelian groups
$$
c^q_{\mathcal F}:H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q(X_{\Et},\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})\qquad(q\geq0),
$$
the left side the cohomology of $\mathcal F$ on $X$ [pqf-def-cohomology], the right side etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], with $c^0_{\mathcal F}$ the identity of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$, such that for every $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of quasi-coherent modules and every $q\geq0$
$$
c^q_{\mathcal G}\circ H^q(X,\varphi)=H^q(X_{\Et},\varphi_{\mathrm{et}})\circ c^q_{\mathcal F}.
$$

source.place: Proposition 03DW (descent-proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent), part (2): canonical isomorphisms $H^q(S,\mathcal F)=H^q(S_\etale,\mathcal F^a)$; also Etale Cohomology, Theorem 03P2 (etale-cohomology-theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: For $u:U\to X$ put $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}(u)=\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$ and for an $X$-morphism $g:U'\to U$ use the pullback restriction $\rho_g$ of [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. The presheaf functoriality statement [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] proves that these restrictions are additive and compose, while [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent] proves the presheaf is a sheaf. Applying the same pullback functor to an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\varphi$ gives the maps $\Gamma(U,u^*\varphi)$; their compatibility with the restrictions is the naturality asserted in the presheaf-functoriality statement, so they define a morphism $\varphi_{\mathrm{et}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves].

source.place: Section 35.8, Tags 03DR and 03DT, equation (35.8.1): the associated etale sheaf and its functoriality

proof.text: Let $\epsilon:X_{\mathrm{Et}}\to X_{\rm Zar}$ be the morphism of sites induced by the inclusion of open subschemes, as in [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-etale-inclusion-morphism-of-sites], so $(\epsilon_*\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})(U)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}(j_U)=\Gamma(U,j_U^*\mathcal F)$ for an open $U\subseteq X$ with inclusion $j_U:U\to X$. Its pullback on cohomology [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] over the final object $X$, followed by $H^q$ of the counit $\epsilon^{-1}\epsilon_*\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$, is the map $e^q:H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\epsilon_*\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})\to H^q(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})$; in degree zero it is the identity of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})$ by the triangle identity. Next, the identification $\epsilon_*\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}\cong\mathcal F_{ab}$, with $\mathcal F_{ab}$ the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal F$ on $X_{\rm Zar}$: for an open $U$ let $\theta_U:\mathcal F(U)=(\mathcal F|_U)(U)\to\Gamma(U,j_U^*\mathcal F)$ be the map on sections over $U$ of the isomorphism $\kappa_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}j_U^*\mathcal F$ of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]; it is an isomorphism of groups, and by the unit clause of that statement (with the open $U$ of $X$) $\theta_U(t)=\eta^{j_U}(t)=j_U^*t$. For opens $W\subseteq U$ with inclusion $g:W\to U$, so $j_W=j_U\circ g$, the restriction of $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$ along $g$ is $\rho_g(s)=c_{g,j_U}(g^*s)$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], and the normalization of $c_{g,j_U}$ by the units in [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] gives $\rho_g(\theta_U(t))=c_{g,j_U}(g^*j_U^*t)=j_W^*t=\eta^{j_W}(t)=\theta_W(t|_W)$, the last equality again by the unit clause of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] (for $j_W$ and the open $U$, $j_W^{-1}U=W$). Hence $\theta:\mathcal F_{ab}\xrightarrow{\sim}\epsilon_*\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves on $X_{\rm Zar}$. For an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ the naturality of $\kappa$ in the module gives $\Gamma(U,j_U^*\varphi)\circ\theta_U=\theta_U\circ\varphi_U$, i.e. $\epsilon_*(\varphi_{\mathrm{et}})\circ\theta=\theta\circ\varphi_{ab}$. Finally [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree] gives $\alpha^q:H^q(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal F_{ab})$. Define $c^q_{\mathcal F}=e^q\circ H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\theta)\circ\alpha^q:H^q(X,\mathcal F)\to H^q(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}})$.

source.place: Proposition 03DW, part (2), and etale-cohomology.tex Lemma 09AX: the comparison map induced by the inclusion of the Zariski site

proof.text: For every affine open $U\subseteq X$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-over-open] identifies the value of the higher-direct-image presheaf with $H^q(U_{\mathrm{Et}},(\mathcal F|_U)_{\mathrm{et}})$, which is zero for $q>0$ by [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent]. Hence the presheaf $P^q(U)=H^q(U_{\mathrm{Et}},(\mathcal F|_U)_{\mathrm{et}})$ is zero on the affine basis. Every open has an affine covering, so the sheafification $ (P^q)^\# $ is zero; the sheafification description [lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] therefore gives $R^q\epsilon_*\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}=0$ for $q>0$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03P2 (theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent), affine case and the preceding Lemma Tag 03P1

proof.text: Apply the Leray degeneration statement [lem-weil-pbc-site-leray-degenerate] to $\epsilon$ and the vanishing of its higher direct images from Step 3. The edge map in that lemma is therefore an isomorphism for every $q$, so the map $e^q$ of Step 2 (the edge map $e^q_{X,\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}}$ for the final object $X$) is an isomorphism, and hence so is $c^q_{\mathcal F}=e^q\circ H^q(\theta)\circ\alpha^q$. This proves the asserted comparison for every scheme, including non-separated schemes.

source.place: Proposition Tag 03DW, proof after the separated case: injective resolutions and the comparison of the two Cech spectral sequences

proof.text: For $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, the naturality square for $c^q$ is the composite of four commuting squares: (i) the naturality square of the module/underlying-abelian comparison [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree]; (ii) $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},-)$ applied to the square $\epsilon_*(\varphi_{\mathrm{et}})\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal G}\circ\varphi_{ab}$ of Step 2; (iii) the naturality square for the site-cohomology pullback [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback]; and (iv) the square for the counit $\epsilon^{-1}\epsilon_*\to\mathrm{id}$, which is natural by the adjunction. Thus $c^q_{\mathcal G}\circ H^q(X,\varphi)=H^q(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\varphi_{\mathrm{et}})\circ c^q_{\mathcal F}$. In degree zero, $e^0$ is the identity by the triangle identity (Step 2) and $\alpha^0$ is the identity by the degree-zero clause of [lem-sc-zariski-module-abelian-cohomology-agree], so $c^0_{\mathcal F}=\theta_X$, which is the identity of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ under the identification $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)=\Gamma(X,\mathrm{id}_X^*\mathcal F)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}(X)$ given by $\kappa$ for $j_X=\mathrm{id}_X$.
